A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QuaSAR work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across additions, renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original reasoning evaluations, fine-tuning experiments, ablations, robustness tests and self-correction results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds benchmark comparisons in Appendix E and a manually assessed error analysis in Appendix J.

M1.justification: The four-stage reasoning procedure, in-context and demonstration-generation applications, filtering procedure, training objective and Appendix A prompting template remain unchanged.

E1.justification: New Appendix E expands evaluated data coverage to MATH, XCOPA and MGSM for GPT-4o and Llama-3-8B, retaining the original benchmark suite. Exact languages and subsets used are unspecified. Section 6's proposed multilingual GSM-Symbolic and retrieval-augmented extensions are future work, not additional evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the original experiments is unchanged, including baseline prompting, CoT, CoMAT, Faithful CoT and FLARE where originally reported. The new benchmarks reuse baseline prompting and CoT without introducing another comparison method.

E3.justification: Appendix J introduces manual assessment of isolated and cumulative stage errors on a GSM-Symbolic ablation subset using GPT-4o. Existing splits, evaluation procedures, model identifiers and tuning budgets remain unchanged. Benchmark-specific protocols for Appendix E are not documented.

E4.justification: Appendix J adds a targeted analysis locating failures across abstraction, formalisation, explanation and answering. Earlier step ablations, robustness tests, training-data scaling, self-correction results and worked examples are retained; the new main-text self-correction discussion does not establish a new experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests. The added stage-error percentages describe outcomes rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 8–9 add complete baseline/CoT/QuaSAR comparisons on three benchmarks for two models; for example, GPT-4o scores 79.5 with QuaSAR versus 76.8 with CoT on MATH. Appendix J adds isolated stage-error rates of 8%, 12%, 16% and 6%, with 36% cumulative pipeline failure on its subset. Original numerical results and plotted values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The reasoning formalisation, Equation 1 training objective and mathematical worked examples are retained. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations are introduced; the new error analysis is empirical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the claims about accuracy, robustness, efficiency and quasi-symbolic reasoning, including the stated accuracy improvement of up to 8%. The conclusion moves from Section 6 to Section 7 without substantive revision.

C2.justification: New Section 6 discusses multilingual alignment and retrieval-augmented knowledge-conflict resolution as future applications. Appendix J adds an interpretation of errors accumulating across reasoning stages. The explanation that structured QuaSAR outputs facilitate correction was already present in v1's final appendix.

D1.justification: v1 Appendix E specifies four Nvidia RTX A6000 GPUs with 48GB VRAM; v2 removes this hardware disclosure. Training hyperparameters, model-version identifiers, generation settings and the promise to release code and data remain. The GPT-4 wording does not establish a model switch because Appendix B already aliases GPT-4o as GPT-4.

R1.justification: Four works are added to connect the paper with multilingual reasoning and retrieval-augmented research in the introduction and new future-work section. The contrastive-explanations reference receives a publication update, while shortening the Llama 3 author list does not remove that cited work. The main related-work discussion remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited wording and spelling corrections, revises author, affiliation and funding information, adds an Additional Analysis paragraph and a Future Works section, and reorganises appendix headings. Most scientific prose, including the conclusion, is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds benchmark Tables 8–9 and the stage-error display in Table 12, rearranges appendix pages 14–15, and relabels the scaling-plot legends as QuaSAR without changing plotted values. Header and bibliography layout also change; existing tables and examples are principally retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The additional benchmark checks and explicit failure breakdown modestly strengthen scrutiny of generality and reasoning failures. Their value is limited by missing benchmark-specific settings and error-analysis sample sizes. These diagnostic gains outweigh the small reproducibility loss from removing hardware information, while leaving the original method and main validation unchanged.
